@@ -731,6 +741,57 @@ class AssertionRewriter(ast.NodeVisitor):
     def is_rewrite_disabled(docstring):
         return "PYTEST_DONT_REWRITE" in docstring
 
+    @staticmethod
+    def unroll_iterable_assert(assert_):
+        """Try to unroll a call to the builtin ``all()`` whose sole
+        argument is a simple generator expression or list comprehension
+        (e.g. ``all(is_even(x) for x in numbers)``) into an equivalent
+        ``for`` loop wrapping an ``assert`` of the individual predicate.
+
+        This gives much more useful failure reports, as they will point
+        out exactly which item of the iterable failed the predicate,
+        rather than just reporting the resulting boolean value of the
+        call to ``all()`` (see issue #5062).
+
+        Returns the new ``ast.For`` node if the transformation could be
+        applied, or ``None`` if the assert should be processed normally
+        (e.g. because it's not a call to ``all()``, or the call is too
+        complex to unroll safely).
+        """
+        test = assert_.test
+        if not (
+            isinstance(test, ast.Call)
+            and isinstance(test.func, ast.Name)
+            and test.func.id == "all"
+            and len(test.args) == 1
+            and not test.keywords
+            and not getattr(test, "starargs", None)
+            and not getattr(test, "kwargs", None)
+            and isinstance(test.args[0], (ast.GeneratorExp, ast.ListComp))
+        ):
+            return None
+
+        gen_exp = test.args[0]
+        if len(gen_exp.generators) != 1:
+            # Multiple ``for`` clauses: keep it simple and don't unroll.
+            return None
+
+        comprehension = gen_exp.generators[0]
+        if comprehension.ifs or getattr(comprehension, "is_async", 0):
+            # ``if`` filters or async generators are not handled here.
+            return None
+
+        inner_assert = ast.Assert(test=gen_exp.elt, msg=assert_.msg)
+        ast.copy_location(inner_assert, assert_)
+        for_loop = ast.For(
+            target=comprehension.target,
+            iter=comprehension.iter,
+            body=[inner_assert],
+            orelse=[],
+        )
+        ast.copy_location(for_loop, assert_)
+        return for_loop
+
